title: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix
oneLiner: The producers' central objection: forced local sales at any price make new fields harder to finance.
body: Australian Energy Producers argued the draft imposed complex and opaque compliance obligations, would undermine trust with Asian buyers, and would deter investment. Santos's chief executive said forcing sales at any price could 'kill companies'; a smaller producer called the scheme 'nationalisation by stealth'. If new supply does not come, the argument runs, prices rise regardless of reservation.
contextBackground: This objection shaped the September softening. It is the industry's position rather than an independent finding, and the industry was itself split: two of the three Queensland ventures accepted reservation.
contextDisagreement: Supporters of the scheme answer that Western Australia reserved gas for twenty years without choking investment, and that producers who already supply the domestic market had no difficulty accepting the rule.

evidenceItems.citation: Mining Weekly (Reuters), 'Australian Energy Producers say gas review falls short on supply goals', 19 May 2026

otherClaim.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices

claimItself.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices
claimItself.oneLiner: Australia has decided to reserve gas for domestic buyers. The question now is whether the scheme, as designed and then softened, will do what it was announced to do.
claimItself.body: In May 2026 the federal government announced that Queensland's three LNG export ventures must reserve a share of export volumes for Australian users from July 2027, with contracts signed before 22 December 2025 exempt. In September 2026 the rule was recast around forecast domestic demand rather than a flat share of exports. The government says prices will fall; it will not say by how much.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Because export contracts signed before 22 December 2025 are exempt, the scheme reaches too little gas to move prices for years

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's

otherClaim.title: Two of the three Queensland LNG ventures accepted a reservation scheme; only Santos opposed it

claimItself.title: Two of the three Queensland LNG ventures accepted a reservation scheme; only Santos opposed it
claimItself.oneLiner: The industry's own split weakens the claim that reservation is unworkable.
claimItself.body: Reporting around the May 2026 announcement described the LNG industry as broadly supportive, chiefly to end ad hoc interventions by successive governments, with Australia Pacific LNG and Shell's QCLNG accepting the policy and Santos's GLNG preferring the status quo. GLNG is also the venture that has drawn most on domestic gas to meet export contracts.
